item.title: #3578168: Streamed chatbot agent response
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 1.2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +498/−10 · php +497/−10 · neon +1
  • Diff: 35d0fef
  • Discussion: #3578168 · 3 contributors · 31 comments
  • Followers: 4
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

AI assistants backed by an AI agent now honor streaming output. Before, calling streamedOutput(TRUE) on an agent-backed assistant had no effect, and the whole response came back as one complete message. Now the response comes back as a streamed iterator, as it does for assistants without an agent.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: AgentRunner::runAsAgent() gains an optional trailing bool $streaming = FALSE parameter.

Technical details

AiAssistantApiRunner::process() now passes $this->streaming as a new last argument to AgentRunner::runAsAgent(). When it is set, runAsAgent() calls setStreamedOutput(TRUE) on the ChatInput it gives the agent. If solve() returns a StreamedChatMessageIteratorInterface, the runner wraps it in a ChatOutput and returns it right away. Its normalized value is the iterator itself.

Persisting the agent thread state in the ai_assistant_threads temp store used to happen before solve(). It moved into a private storeAgentState() method. For streamed responses it runs from a callback registered with $response->addCallback(), so state is saved or deleted only once the stream completes. Non-streaming runs call it right after solve(). If the agent is not finished, the state is saved. Otherwise it is deleted.

The commit adds unit tests: AgentRunnerStreamingTest and AiAssistantApiRunnerAgentStreamingTest. The issue's remaining-tasks list also names a check of agents that need several LLM or tool-call loops before the final streamed answer. The diff has no test for that.

Upgrade

Existing callers of runAsAgent() need no change, because the new parameter defaults to FALSE. To stream from code that calls it directly:

$output = $agent_runner->runAsAgent($assistant_id, $chat_history, $defaults, $job_id, FALSE, [], TRUE);

item.title: #3585956: ResourceContentCache reuses the first caller's cache-context variation for every later caller
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +189/−76 · php +167/−56 · md +14/−18 · yml +8/−2
  • Diff: 69467c2
  • Discussion: #3585956 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

MCP resource content cached for one user could be returned to other users. A resource that varied by a cache context such as user kept serving the first caller's content to everyone with view access until the entry expired. Access checks still ran on every call, so the leak only affected users who were allowed to read the resource. Each caller now gets the cached variation for their own context values.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Cached MCP resource content could be served to a different user than the one it was generated for, when the content varied by cache context (e.g. user) and both users had view access.

Technical details

The old ResourceContentCache::generate() stored the first caller's resolved context keys (for example [user]=10) in a pointer entry at mcp_resource:{uri}. It reused that suffix for every later lookup. Render caching avoids this by storing context tokens and resolving them again on each request.

The class now delegates storage to core's VariationCacheInterface, the store RenderCache uses. It is wired as a new service, mcp_server.variation_cache.resource, created from variation_cache_factory over the default bin. The mcp_server.resource_content_cache service takes only that service as its argument, so the constructor no longer takes cache.default and cache_contexts_manager. Cache keys are ['mcp_resource', hash('sha256', $expandedUri)]. The URI is hashed because it is client-controlled and the variation cache joins keys and context keys with :, so a raw URI could spell another caller's cache ID. The access result's cacheability is passed as the initial cacheability to both get() and set(), and it is merged into the DTO metadata.

Behavior that stays the same: the access callback runs on every call and is never cached, and a NULL from the content callback raises ResourceNotFoundException. Content with max-age 0 is not stored. A new kernel test, ResourceContentCacheTest, covers two users reading one resource, the URI-spoofing case, and max-age 0.

Upgrade

Previously cached resource content sits under the old mcp_resource:{uri} pointer keys, which the new code does not read, so it is simply ignored. Clear caches if you want those stale entries removed. Code that constructs ResourceContentCache directly must pass a VariationCacheInterface instead of the cache backend and contexts manager. The class is final and used through the mcp_server.resource_content_cache service.

item.title: #3585953: Created content timestamp uses mcp server start time
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 6 files, +173/−2 · php +160 · yml +9 · md +4/−2
  • Diff: 7d981c7
  • Discussion: #3585953 · 1 contributor · 12 comments

Summary

When the MCP server runs over STDIO (drush mcp:server), content edits made by an AI client were stamped with the time the client connected, not the time of the edit. This affected entity changed times, revision creation times and comment created times. Each STDIO message now gets the current time as its request time, so timestamps are correct for the whole session. HTTP transport was never affected.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

drush mcp:server is one long-lived PHP process, so Drupal's request time, read from the initial request's REQUEST_TIME, never advanced. The fix adds Drupal\mcp_server\EventSubscriber\StdioRequestTimeSubscriber, registered as mcp_server.stdio_request_time_subscriber with @request_stack. It subscribes to the MCP SDK's Mcp\Event\RequestEvent at priority 1000, so other listeners already see the new time.

When PHP_SAPI === 'cli', it sets REQUEST_TIME and REQUEST_TIME_FLOAT on the current request's server bag. It also sets them in $_SERVER, because core's time service falls back to $_SERVER when there is no request. Under any other SAPI it does nothing, since each HTTP message is already its own request. A kernel test, StdioRequestTimeTest, backdates the request time and checks that both initialize and ping messages move it forward.

item.title: #3585955: Concurrent requests on one session get 503 "MCP session lock timeout" after a lost lock race
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 9 files, +271/−9 · php +267/−6 · md +3/−3 · yml +1
  • Diff: 65bce47
  • Discussion: #3585955 · 1 contributor · 11 comments

Summary

When an MCP client sent several requests at once on the same session (for example resources/read, resources/list and tools/list), some of them could fail immediately with a 503 "MCP session lock timeout" even though no real timeout had happened. Requests that lose the race for the session lock now keep waiting, up to 30 seconds in total, and only get a 503 if the lock really stays busy that long. The reporter's test went from 2 failures in 90 requests to 270 of 270 passing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: LockBackendSessionLock takes the datetime.time service as a new third constructor argument.

Technical details

LockBackendInterface::wait() returns as soon as the lock looks free. With three or more concurrent requests, two waiters can see it free, one takes it, and the other's single follow-up acquire() fails at once. LockBackendSessionLock::acquire() now loops on acquire() against one deadline of WAIT_SECONDS (30), computed from TimeInterface::getCurrentMicroTime(). Each wait() gets only the remaining time, rounded up to whole seconds. A TRUE return from wait() means the lock stayed held for the whole delay, so it throws SessionLockTimeoutException, which the SDK answers with a 503. A FALSE return means the lock looked free, so the loop retries acquire(). Retrying acquire() once more was rejected because it only moves the race. Restarting a full 30 s wait() each time was rejected because it could hold a worker without limit.

The loop lives in LockBackendSessionLock, the SessionLockInterface adapter the SDK calls for every locked request. The issue says an earlier patch with a separate SessionLock class was dropped in favor of this. The service definition gains @datetime.time as a third argument. The commit adds unit tests (LockBackendSessionLockRaceTest, with FakeClock and ContendedLockBackend helpers) covering a free lock, lost races, a shared budget and a long hold. The kernel test constructors were updated for the new argument.

Upgrade

Rebuild caches after updating, because the mcp_server.session_lock service definition gained an argument. Code that constructs LockBackendSessionLock directly must pass the time service as the third argument:

new LockBackendSessionLock($lock, $database, $this->container->get('datetime.time'))

item.title: #3586769: Full chat thread pool deletes the conversation in slot 0 on every new thread and carries over previous conversation context
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +149/−21 · php +149/−21
  • Diff: 0a8127b
  • Discussion: #3586769 · 1 contributor · 10 comments

Summary

For AI assistants using the private_tempstore_pool chat history mode, once a user had 11 open threads (for example by refreshing the chatbot page instead of using Clear History), every chat request deleted their conversation in slot 0. Old conversation context could also leak into the new thread. Now a full pool evicts the least recently used thread only when a new thread is actually needed, and the evicted thread's stored contexts are cleared too.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

AiAssistantApiRunner::setAssistant() used to call generateUniqueKey() immediately. Access checks, AiAssistantApiProcessor::initializeRunner() and ResetSession all call setAssistant() before the client's own thread id is set. With a full pool, each of those requests evicted slot 0. The eager generation is removed. The runner now reads its thread id through getThreadsKey() everywhere it previously used $this->threadId (message history, output contexts, structured results, assistant message building, action instances), so a key is only generated when one is needed.

In generateUniqueKey(), a full pool now evicts the slot whose last message has the oldest timestamp, instead of always assistant_thread_{uid}_0. Slots with no messages count as timestamp 0. The evicted key is also removed from the runner's temp store (getTempStore()->delete($evicted_key)), so output_contexts and structured_results from the previous conversation no longer carry over. A new kernel test, AiAssistantApiRunnerThreadPoolTest, covers both behaviors.

item.title: #3585954: Replace SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport with the SDK's session lock
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +665/−550 · php +629/−515 · md +26/−23 · yml +9/−11 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 41b50f6
  • Discussion: #3585954 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

mcp_server 2.x now requires mcp/sdk 0.9 or later, and drops support for 0.7 and 0.8. Per-session request serialization is no longer done by module code in the HTTP controller and a custom transport. The SDK's own session lock now does it, backed by Drupal's lock service. The change also fixes tool input schemas that Tool API writes with an empty properties map (an \ArrayObject), which the SDK's Tool class would not accept.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: mcp/sdk constraint changed from ^0.7.1 || ^0.8 to ^0.9; 0.7 and 0.8 are no longer supported.
  • API change: The mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service (tagged mcp_server.transport_middleware) is removed. McpServerController no longer takes the lock or database services.
  • New API: New mcp_server.session_lock service, Drupal\mcp_server\Session\LockBackendSessionLock, implementing the SDK's SessionLockInterface.

Technical details

McpServerFactory takes a new SessionLockInterface argument and passes it to Builder::setSessionLock(). The implementation is LockBackendSessionLock, registered as mcp_server.session_lock with the lock and database services. It keeps the lock name mcp_session:<sha256 of session id>. acquire() waits once and then throws the SDK's SessionLockTimeoutException. tryAcquire() is for the SDK's SSE polls. release() is deferred while Connection::inTransaction() is true, because a rollback would restore the deleted semaphore row. This keeps the old behavior for a tool that suspends inside a transaction.

SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport, which overrode protected SDK hooks, is deleted. So are its lock handling in McpServerController::handle() and the PassThroughMiddleware class. The controller now builds the SDK's StreamableHttpTransport and passes the SDK's PassthroughMiddleware when no middleware is tagged. SSE responses are still converted to streamed Symfony responses. A lock timeout is now answered by the SDK (503 with a JSON-RPC error), not by ServiceUnavailableHttpException.

The 0.7/0.8 compatibility code is also removed. That covers the method_exists() guards around setRequestState(), McpServerServiceProvider::alter(), and the mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service. FiberShield now recognizes the SDK's RequestSuspension and NotificationSuspension objects, where it used to look for an array with a type key. McpServerFactory converts an \ArrayObject schema map to an array. A test_array_object_input tool was added to mcp_server_test to cover that. The CI lowest-SDK job and the contributor docs now pin ^0.9.

Upgrade

Update the constraint in composer.json:

"mcp/sdk": "^0.9"

Code that tags or references mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version, or constructs McpServerController directly with the lock and database arguments, needs updating. The SDK's transport already applies ProtocolVersionMiddleware to handshake-era requests.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: October 22, 2026
  • Committed: October 28, 2026 (5 days later)

item.title: #3585949: Allow mcp/sdk ^0.9
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +665/−550 · php +629/−515 · md +26/−23 · yml +9/−11 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 41b50f6
  • Discussion: #3585949 · 1 contributor · 17 comments

Summary

mcp_server 2.x now requires mcp/sdk 0.9 and no longer installs with 0.7 or 0.8. Update with composer update mcp/sdk --with-all-dependencies when you update the module. The issue's release notes say 0.9 rejects tool results that don't match a tool's outputSchema, so custom tools with a mismatched schema will start returning errors. The issue says 0.9 also fixes concurrent SSE streams of one session taking each other's client responses, and stateless SSE output buffering that kept Claude Code from connecting.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The commit raises the floor in composer.json and pins the composer (lowest SDK) CI job to ^0.9. It also removes the code that handled 0.7 and 0.8: the method_exists() guards, the mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service, and McpServerServiceProvider::alter(). The controller now passes the SDK's own PassthroughMiddleware when no middleware is tagged, replacing the deleted Transport\PassThroughMiddleware.

Session locking moved from the controller into the SDK. McpServerController no longer takes a lock, and SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport is deleted. McpServerFactory passes the new LockBackendSessionLock to Builder::setSessionLock(). It uses the same lock name as before, mcp_session: plus the sha256 of the session id. It throws SessionLockTimeoutException when the lock can't be acquired. The SDK holds the lock around session reads and saves, and releases it while a tool waits on the client. If a tool suspends inside a database transaction, the release is deferred until the transaction ends, because a rollback would restore the semaphore row. The issue says 0.9 saves a resumed tool's session inside the fiber resume, which only the SDK's lock covers.

Other adaptations to 0.9: FiberShield now re-yields RequestSuspension and NotificationSuspension objects instead of arrays with a type key. McpServerFactory converts an ArrayObject schema map, such as the empty properties map Tool API writes, to an array so the SDK's Tool accepts it. A new test tool, test_array_object_input, covers that case. Tests that fed StdioTransport from php://memory now use tmpfile(), since the transport calls stream_select() on stdin.

Upgrade

Update the SDK together with the module:

composer update mcp/sdk --with-all-dependencies

Custom tools that declare an outputSchema must return results that match it, or 0.9 will return errors. Code that referenced Drupal\mcp_server\Transport\PassThroughMiddleware should use Mcp\Server\Transport\Http\Middleware\PassthroughMiddleware instead.

item.title: #3585946: Concurrent tool calls on one session can receive each other's elicitation answers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 2.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 31 files, +665/−550 · php +629/−515 · md +26/−23 · yml +9/−11 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 41b50f6
  • Discussion: #3585946 · 1 contributor · 5 comments

Summary

The issue reported that two tool calls eliciting on the same MCP session could receive each other's answers. The proposed fix was to wait for an upstream fix in the PHP SDK (php-sdk#544) and then add a test. The shipped commit raises the SDK requirement to mcp/sdk ^0.9 only. The SDK now owns the per-session locking that this module used to do itself. Sites need an SDK 0.9 install, and 0.7 and 0.8 are no longer supported. The commit does not include the end to end test with two eliciting tool calls that the issue proposed.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Requirements: mcp/sdk constraint changes from ^0.7.1 || ^0.8 to ^0.9; 0.7 and 0.8 are no longer supported.
  • API change: The mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service is removed, and the mcp_server.session_lock service is added. Calling code that referenced mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version must stop doing so.

Technical details

The module's own locking is replaced by SDK hooks. McpServerController no longer takes a Drupal lock around the whole run, and it no longer wraps the SSE stream callback to release the lock. It builds the SDK's own StreamableHttpTransport. The custom SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport, which overrode getOutgoingMessages(), checkForResponse() and handleFiberYield(), is deleted. So is the PassThroughMiddleware class, replaced by the SDK's PassthroughMiddleware.

The new Drupal\mcp_server\Session\LockBackendSessionLock implements the SDK's SessionLockInterface (acquire(), tryAcquire(), release()) on Drupal's lock service. It uses the lock name mcp_session:<sha256 of session id>, as before. acquire() waits once and retries, then throws the SDK's SessionLockTimeoutException. If a tool suspends inside a database transaction, release() is deferred until the transaction ends, because a release inside it would be invisible to other requests and a rollback would restore the semaphore row. The service is mcp_server.session_lock, passed to McpServerFactory, which calls Builder::setSessionLock().

Other changes: FiberShield now recognises the SDK's RequestSuspension and NotificationSuspension objects instead of arrays with a type key. McpServerFactory calls setRequestState() unconditionally. It also converts an empty ArrayObject schema map (as Tool API writes it) to an array before building the SDK Tool. The mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service and McpServerServiceProvider::alter() are removed, because the 0.9 transport applies that middleware itself. CI's lowest-SDK job now pins ^0.9. Tests that hit StdioTransport now use tmpfile() for stdin, since the transport's stream_select() rejects php://memory.

Upgrade

Update the SDK constraint in composer.json:

"mcp/sdk": "^0.9"

Custom code that referenced the mcp_server.middleware.protocol_version service, Drupal\mcp_server\Transport\PassThroughMiddleware or SessionLockingStreamableHttpTransport must stop using them. Use Mcp\Server\Transport\Http\Middleware\PassthroughMiddleware and the SDK's StreamableHttpTransport instead.

item.title: #3586702: Emit automator config ID tag and entity_context on chat requests
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586702 · 1 contributor · 23 comments

Summary

Chat requests sent by AI Automators now identify which automator config entity produced them. Previously, several automators on the same field (for example Default, Short summary and Bullet outline on one body field) sent identical tags, so event subscribers could not tell them apart. Requests now also carry structured entity information, including for unsaved entities where the entity ID is not yet known.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New ai_automator:id:{automator config ID} tag and entity_context request metadata (entity_type, entity_id, uuid, bundle, field_name, automator_id) on automator chat requests; new protected RuleBase::buildEntityContext() and attachEntityContext().

Technical details

AiAutomatorEntityModifier::entityHasConfig() and RunAutomatorAction now set $automatorConfig['id'] to the automator config entity ID. In entityHasConfig() this is set after the plugin config loop so a stray automator_id setting cannot override it. RuleBase::getTags() emits ai_automator:id:{id} when id is a non-empty string, alongside the existing ai_automator, type, entity_type, entity, bundle and field_name tags.

New protected methods RuleBase::buildEntityContext() and attachEntityContext() set an entity_context request metadata value on the ChatInput via setRequestMetadataValue(). The array holds entity_type, entity_id (NULL when isNew()), uuid, bundle, field_name and automator_id; nothing is attached when there is no entity. It is attached in runRawChatMessage() after applyGuardrailsToInput(), since that may return a clone of the input, and also in the vision call in RichTextImageDescriptionTrait. Kernel and unit tests were added, and docs/modules/ai_automators/index.md documents the tags.

Upgrade

Subscribers that need to target one automator can match on the tag, e.g. ai_automator:id:node.blog.field_content.bullet_outline, or read entity_context from the request metadata. Custom code that builds its own $automatorConfig array and calls getTags() should set $automatorConfig['id'] to get the tag.

item.title: #3594806: Show the input and the model's answer when reviewing recorded decisions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594806 · 1 contributor · 4 comments

Summary

AI Eval's Review decisions screen can now show the reviewer the text the model judged, not just a link to the entity. This is opt-in per caller on Record decisions and is off by default, because the text can contain personal data. When enabled, the text appears in a collapsed section on each row and is removed after the answer is reviewed or when its entity is deleted. The model's probability stays hidden while an answer waits for review, so it does not bias the label. A separate view of reviewed answers shows the saved label next to the raw probability and, if a calibration was applied, the calibrated one. This summary is based on the issue text only. The fix's code was not available to check, so the shipped behavior may differ in detail.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Database update: Nullable text column for the stored state on ai_eval_decision_record, with an update hook (as described in the issue).
  • Config change: Record decisions gets a per-caller opt-in, "Keep the text sent to the model, for review", off by default (as described in the issue).
  • Permission change: Stored text is shown only to users with the existing review permission.

Technical details

The issue explains why the text is stored instead of rebuilt from the entity reference. A token-mode automator sends a rendered token prompt. A multi-value base field sends one request per value, and the record does not keep which value. A caller that is not a field automator has no entity field. The entity can also change after the answer. The plan is to store the sent text in a nullable column on ai_eval_decision_record, added by an update hook. The existing entity-deletion cleanup hook would delete it, as would the review step. The issue lists the retention rule as unconfirmed: delete after review, or keep until a calibration is fitted from the answer. It also lists tests for storage, deletion and access, and an update to the privacy text on Record decisions. The reviewed-answers view is meant to let each answer type render its own output: true/false now, choice and score later. I could not find the implementing commit in the cloned repository, so these details come from the issue body, not from a diff.

Upgrade

Run database updates after upgrading to add the nullable column on ai_eval_decision_record. Then decide per caller on Record decisions whether to turn on "Keep the text sent to the model, for review". It is off by default. Update your privacy notice if you enable it.

item.title: #3594822: Failure mode rates count each reviewer's annotation of the same question
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594822 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

Failure mode counts and rates for a result or test now count each reviewed question once. Before, if two reviewers annotated the same question, its failure mode was counted twice and the total grew by two. Now only the earliest annotation for each question counts. On sites with more than one reviewer per question, counts and percentages in the failure modes table will change. The user docs now define Count as questions whose counted annotation carries that mode.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New public static AnnotationStore::joinCanonical() limits an annotation query to the earliest row per (result_id, question_id).

Technical details

FailureRateService::aggregate() ran COUNT(*) over every annotation row in scope, which ratesForResult() and ratesForTarget() both use. It now calls a new static helper, AnnotationStore::joinCanonical(), before the GROUP BY failure_mode. The helper is the SQL form of AnnotationStore::canonical(). It joins a subquery that takes MIN(id) per (result_id, question_id) over the whole annotation table. The service filters on that join, so the earliest annotation per question is the one counted.

The earliest row is chosen across the whole table, not only the filtered rows. A condition added by the caller, such as the ratesForTarget() time window ($sinceTimestamp), therefore filters out the counted row. It does not promote a later reviewer's row. The total used for rates is now the number of annotated questions in the scope. This matches the rule judge validation and calibration already use, and the reviewed-traces rates, which already kept one earliest label per conversation.

This is reported from the 1.1.x branch. I did not find a commit or MR reference in the issue thread, which has no comments.

Disabling a failure mode in AI Eval now retires it. Before, the Status checkbox did nothing: a disabled mode was still offered to annotators, saved onto annotations, and exported. Now a disabled mode no longer appears in the annotation form or the trace review verdict bar, and a request that picks one is refused with a "not saved" message. Labels that already use the mode keep it and show "(disabled)". Failure rates still count them and mark the row "(disabled)". A taxonomy export leaves disabled modes out. The docs now recommend disabling over deleting, because deleting leaves labels pointing at a mode that no longer exists.

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AnnotationStore::save() and LabelStore::saveGroup() now throw \InvalidArgumentException for a disabled or unknown failure mode. Their constructors, and those of EvalResultsController and TraceReviewController, take a ReferenceOptions argument.
  • New API: ReferenceOptions::failureModes(?string $keep = NULL) lists the failure modes a label may carry.

Technical details

The fix adds ReferenceOptions::failureModes(?string $keep = NULL). It returns enabled modes sorted by weight then label. If $keep names a disabled mode, the one the label already carries, it is also listed as "<label> (disabled)" so a re-save keeps it. EvalResultsController::annotationFormBuild() and TraceReviewController use it instead of an unfiltered loadMultiple().

Enforcement is server-side as well as in the select. AnnotationStore::save() and LabelStore::saveGroup() now take ReferenceOptions as a constructor argument. They throw \InvalidArgumentException for a failure mode that is unknown, or disabled and not already on that record. The annotation endpoint checks the mode before saving. It returns HTTP 200 with a visible error and does not return a 4xx, because htmx does not swap 4xx responses. It also keeps a 400 for an invalid verdict. In the trace review verdict bar, typing a new mode name that matches a disabled mode is refused. The matching logic is split into matchFailureMode() and createFailureMode().

FailureModeTaxonomySerializer::export() skips modes where status() is false. The schema carries no status key. Import never changes the status of an existing mode, and a new mode is created enabled. The commit adds it to the AnnotationStore and LabelStore definitions in ai_eval.services.yml, and to the EvalResultsController and TraceReviewController constructors. item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal feature request
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594811 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

AI Eval results for agent-mode tests now record which model answered and how many tokens it used, as chat-mode tests already did. Before this, an agent row showed "not recorded", so its cost could not be compared with a chat or workflow test on the same questions. Judge calls are not counted, and a failed answer still gets the figures.

While an agent answers one question, a new shared ModelCallRecorder event subscriber (service ai_eval.model_call_recorder) is armed in EvalRunner::runQuestionBody() and records each chat provider call as a ModelCall. It is armed only for mode === 'agent'. It is disarmed in the finally block before the graders run, so judge calls never count. The recorder is shared with the AI Answers recording from #3594802.

The new applyAgentTelemetry() follows the chat-mode meaning of the keys. token_usage (input, output, and optional cached) is written only when the totals are known. ModelCallRecorder::total() returns nothing when any call reports no usage. model_id and model_id_resolved are written only when every call agrees (ModelCallRecorder::shared()). It is applied on both the success path and the failed-answer path. Retries made by the rate limit handler are included in the recorded calls. cached_tokens was also added to lastGeneration, so chat and workflow rows now carry an optional token_usage.cached. docs/user/usage/scoring.md and CHANGELOG.md are updated.

The EvalRunner constructor gets an optional trailing ?ModelCallRecorder $modelCallRecorder argument, wired in ai_eval.services.yml. The result row keys are the existing chat-mode keys, so there is no schema change.

Results from AI Answers targets in AI Eval now show which provider and model wrote each answer and how many tokens it used. Before this, those results had no model calls, so cost could not be compared with agent or prompt targets on the same questions. The "answered by" check, which flags a provider serving a different model than requested, also never ran for them. Calls are recorded when an answer fails too. item.title: #3594808: Let a test mark a grader as must pass, so its failure fails the question
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal unknown (0)
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3594808 · 1 contributor · 3 comments

Summary

A test in AI Eval can now mark individual graders as must pass. If a must-pass grader scores a question below the question pass threshold, that question fails, however well the other graders scored. Previously a failing safety check could be outweighed in the average (scores of 5, 5, 5 and 0 average 3.75 and pass). A must-pass failure also fails the whole quality gate, whether the gate metric is average score or pass rate. A must-pass grader that does not apply to a question (no score) does not fail it. The option is a "Must pass" checkbox per selected grader on the test edit form and in the guided test. The results page, the review step and the Drush run output name the must-pass grader that failed each question. Runs with different must-pass lists are not treated as directly comparable.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: New must_pass sequence of grader plugin IDs on the ai_eval.target.* config entity (added to the schema and to EvalTarget config_export), empty by default.
  • API change: ScorerInterface::scoreQuestion() gains a fifth optional parameter array $mustPass = []; custom implementations of the interface must add it.
  • New API: New Scorer::mustPassFailures() static helper, EvalTarget::getMustPass(), and a must_pass_failures key in scoreTarget() and runner results.

Technical details

Scorer::scoreQuestion() converts each grader score to the 0 to 5 composite scale as before. A must-pass grader whose composite score (rounded to two decimals) is below the question pass threshold is added to a must_pass_failed list on the question score, and passed becomes false. A null score adds no failure. A grader error still marks the question errored and takes it out of the gate. Scorer::scoreTarget() calls the new static Scorer::mustPassFailures(), which skips unscored questions but keeps measured failures on questions that errored for another grader. Any such failure forces passed_gate to false for both avg_score and pass_rate metrics. This settles the open question in the issue about the run gate. The threshold used is the shared question pass threshold. The issue's alternative of a separate threshold per grader was not implemented.

must_pass is stored on the EvalTarget entity. getMustPass() returns only ids that are also in graders. It is written to the run snapshot as must_pass in EvalRunner. When a run is resumed or replayed, applySnapshotToConfig() uses the snapshot value. A snapshot without the key, or a resumed run without a snapshot, is treated as an empty list, so older runs score as before. RunComparability compares the sorted lists, and a difference is reported under must_pass. ResultEnvelopeBuilder adds must_pass as a comma-separated string in metric_config.additional_details, next to graders. The form element is built by the new MustPassChoice class, shared by EvalTargetForm and GuidedTestForm. Its checkboxes only show for selected graders, and submitted values for unselected graders are dropped.

Upgrade

Code that implements ScorerInterface must accept the new optional parameter:

public function scoreQuestion(string $questionId, string $input, array $gradeResults, float $questionPassThreshold = 3.5, array $mustPass = []): array;

Existing tests need no config change. must_pass defaults to an empty list, so scoring is unchanged until a grader is marked.

item.title: #3586619: Hide context items and usage records from JSON:API
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal task
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586619 · 1 contributor · 13 comments

Summary

In AI Context (CCC) 1.0.0, context items and usage records are no longer available through core JSON:API. Before, a site that enabled JSON:API let every account with Use Published AI Context in AI Features page through all published context items over HTTP and read their raw fields, without the CCC delivery rules and without usage being recorded. Sites that read or synced items through JSON:API (for example with Entity Share) lose that access, and 1.0.0 has no supported replacement. Run drush cr after updating, because the resources stay available until caches are rebuilt. Core REST can still be enabled on purpose for context items, but no longer offers usage records. If you enabled a REST resource for usage records, delete it before rebuilding the router.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Removes a bulk JSON:API read path that let any account with Use Published AI Context in AI Features page through all published context items with raw fields, bypassing CCC delivery rules.
  • Config change: A site that enabled a core REST resource for usage records must delete rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage before drush cr or drush updatedb, or the router rebuild fails.

Technical details

ai_context_usage now has internal = TRUE in its @ContentEntityType annotation, so JSON:API, core REST discovery and other integrations that skip internal entity types ignore it. A side effect noted in the release note is that Workspaces now ignores usage records, so usage is also recorded while a non-default workspace is active.

ai_context_item is deliberately not marked internal, because Content Moderation and Workspaces skip internal entity types and the flag would remove the editorial workflow and moderation transition access checks. Instead, a new @internal subscriber, AiContextJsonApiResourceTypeSubscriber (registered as ai_context.jsonapi_resource_type_subscriber), listens to the string event name jsonapi.resource_type.build at priority 1000 and calls disableResourceType() for resource types whose name starts with ai_context_item--. Using the string event name means it works when JSON:API is not installed. No post-update is added; drush cr rebuilds the container, entity type definitions and JSON:API resource types.

A kernel test, AiContextEntityExposureTest, checks that with JSON:API enabled both resource types are internal and the user type is not, and that items keep the moderation handler. Docs changed in access-boundaries.md (new "Generic entity APIs" section and updated permission titles), api-stability.md (output of generic entity APIs such as core REST or the serializer is not public API; the scope field section is renamed "normalized shape") and configuration.md. The issue plans an opt-in for context items later (#3586600), which would need a dedicated read permission (#3586357).

Upgrade

After updating, rebuild caches so the container and JSON:API resource types pick up the change:

drush cr

If the site enabled a core REST resource for usage records, delete it first, before drush cr or drush updatedb, and remove it from config sync:

drush config:delete rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage

Also remove rest.resource.entity.ai_context_usage.yml from the config sync directory. Otherwise the router rebuild fails because the REST plugin for usage records no longer exists.

item.title: #3586489: Remove stale consumer config when a host entity is deleted
item.description:
• Project: Drupal AI
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Status: Fixed
  • Discussion: #3586489 · 1 contributor · 14 comments

Summary

Deleting an AI Automator now removes its automator:{id} row from ai_context.consumers. Before this, only deleting an ai_agent did that, and a deleted automator showed up as a stale entry in the consumers listing until an admin removed it by hand. Consumer types from other modules can now get the same cleanup by declaring which entity type hosts them. A consumer type that fails to load is now skipped and logged instead of breaking entity deletes, the consumers listing, or routing.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: AiContextConsumerTypeInterface gains a required method; plugins that implement the interface directly instead of extending AiContextConsumerTypeBase must add it.
  • New API: AiContextConsumerTypeInterface::getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity() and a host_entity_type key on the AiContextConsumerType attribute.

Technical details

ai_context_entity_delete() no longer special-cases ai_agent. It calls a new AiContextConsumerTypeManager::getConsumerIdsForDeletedEntity(), which is marked @internal. That method asks every discovered consumer type plugin, including disabled or unavailable ones, because a leftover row can exist after a kill switch. Each returned ID goes to the existing AiContextScopeCleanupService::removeDeletedConsumerConfig(), so there is no second write path.

Each type answers through the new getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity(EntityInterface $entity): ?AiContextConsumerId method. AiContextConsumerTypeBase implements the 1:1 case from the new host_entity_type attribute argument. If the entity type matches and the ID is non-empty, it returns {plugin_id}:{entity_id}. Otherwise it returns NULL. The agent and automator plugins set host_entity_type to ai_agent and ai_automator. Types with a different ID scheme override the method. Types with no host omit the key.

AiContextConsumerTypeManager::getConsumerTypePlugins() now catches \Exception (not \Error) from createInstance(). It logs the failure and omits that type. The same applies to the mapping call. This is why a broken type is also dropped from the listing and from routing. The manager takes a new optional $logger argument, wired to @logger.channel.ai_context in ai_context.services.yml. No config dependencies were added on ai_context.consumers, and rows that are already stale are not cleaned up retroactively.

Upgrade

Plugins that extend AiContextConsumerTypeBase need no change. A type whose instances are 1:1 with a host entity can opt in through the attribute:

#[AiContextConsumerType(
  id: 'automator',
  // label and description omitted
  host_entity_type: 'ai_automator',
)]

Types with a different ID scheme should override getConsumerIdForDeletedEntity(). Do not gate it on isEnabled() or isAvailable(). Return NULL when the type does not own the entity.
